references.observation: MuseScore's handbook documents distinct note-entry and rest-entry modes, keyboard and mouse pitch entry, and a visible note-entry cursor.
references.principle: Writing musical pitches should remain direct and reversible, with mode distinction made visible rather than hiding an editor gesture.
references.application: Each pitch/time cell toggles the note of an instrument; a separate drawing-mode button makes drag-to-paint distinct from horizontal score navigation.
references.avoid: Do not copy MuseScore's notation editor layout or licensed visual assets; retain a simplified folk-specific modal grid.

references.observation: The MIDI Association describes time-stamped MIDI data streams, tracks and tempo information as the interchange basis for a Standard MIDI File.
references.principle: Export editable musical events with explicit tempo and distinct track streams instead of calling raw audio a MIDI score.
references.application: Export a type-1 MIDI file with six independent instrument tracks, a tempo meta track, note durations and instrument program changes.
references.avoid: Do not present MIDI as recorded instrument audio or promise that different synthesizers use the exact same timbre.

references.observation: MDN documents the modular audio context, oscillators, gain envelopes, filters and accurate scheduling for sequencers.
references.principle: Use browser-native scheduled voices so playback, stopping and local export have one consistent event model and no CDN.
references.application: The app schedules generated folk motifs ahead using AudioContext and renders WAV off-thread through OfflineAudioContext when supported.
references.avoid: Do not pretend generic oscillators are sampled medieval instruments; the release notes call them synthesized approximations.

concepts.medium: Native browser DOM and CSS parchment score with a bespoke editable vector fiddle-and-manuscript icon.
concepts.composition: Score occupies a broad central parchment work surface; selectable instrument rail and musical alchemy flanks keep meaningful controls near their object.
concepts.interaction: Tap individual pitch cells, optionally draw a note contour, change section or voice and instantly audition a four-part folk composition.
concepts.motion: An immediate ink stamp marks each new pitch, and the playing time cursor follows the notes while the section changes.
concepts.rationale: Chosen because the main product experience is interacting with a musical manuscript, not controlling a general-purpose workstation.

concepts.medium: 3D canvas gramophone and wooden cylindrical step-sequencer with physically rotating pegs.
concepts.composition: Large perspective music box in the center with instrument slots around a cylindrical spool and hidden advanced settings.
concepts.interaction: Rotate the wheel, punch note holes and hear mechanical tones until a wax record is complete.
concepts.motion: A motor spins continuously while peg impacts trigger note gates and mechanical gestures.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because three-dimensional peg precision would be unreliable on touch screens, and a constant animation conflicts with long editing sessions.

concepts.medium: Vector-illustrated ink landscape with villages and ruins as music arrangement waypoints.
concepts.composition: Full-width medieval road map where separate landmarks represent tracks, sections and resulting music variations.
concepts.interaction: Travel the road, choose landmarks and generate chapters of a song through narrative decisions.
concepts.motion: The journey pans a map as verses appear at different geographic destinations.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because musical editing would be hidden behind spatial travel and lack the exact note control promised in the core experience.

selection.reason: The note editing grid remains immediately visible on phones and desktop, lets users hear the result of every change, and makes composition feel like writing a living songbook.

rejected.reason: The motor and 3D control geometry would make tactile note input imprecise and increase hardware demand.
A travel narrative would sacrifice predictable pitch/time control and hide actual editable score data.

tools.reason: The source icon is authored in plain SVG and stored within the application repository for deterministic local rendering.
Web Audio nodes and OfflineAudioContext provide locally generated playback and WAV export without external services.
Native layout, responsive CSS and pointer events render the manuscript score with no remote images or build dependencies.

assets.role: Original letterless fiddle silhouette on an illuminated notation page, used for the launcher shortcut and installed application icon.
assets.acceptance: Readably distinct from app text at 48px and consistent with its cream, forest green and terracotta working palette.
assets.integration: Manifest, HTML favicon and scoped offline Service Worker cache reference icons/icon.svg directly.
assets.provenance: Original hand-authored vector geometry created for this application with no third-party image or licensed instrument photograph.

risks: iPhone portrait must permit horizontal score scrolling without accidentally drawing notes; drawing mode must retain precise pointer cancellation.
Large score grids must not push primary transport buttons outside the first viewport.
Progressive WAV export must not freeze normal music state after a failed offline-audio render.
comparisons: Capture 390x844 portrait initial, score edit and playback highlight states; compare against desktop 1366x768 to check dominant score size.
Compare Folkarium's manuscript score against sin-guion's lesson stage and rivals-dna's quiz spread for spatial identity and text density.
